title: Grateful Dead Live at McFarlin Auditorium, S.M.U. on 1969-12-26

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording of a historic acoustic‑electric transition show with a smoking Dark Star, stellar New Speedway Boogie and standout Lovelight
ai_review.review: This archive capture showcases the Grateful Dead’s rare early‑‘69 acoustic set followed by an electric second half that builds into a high‑energy climax. Reviewers rave about the crystal‑clear acoustic guitars, Tom Constanten’s organ work and Garcia’s classic 1969 tone, while noting a few tape cuts in the middle of Rain and Snow/China Cat. The performance shines on Dark Star, New Speedway Boogie and an unforgettable Lovelight, making it one of the most prized late‑’69 shows.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (20+) are 4–5 stars and praise both the musical performance and recording clarity; only a few minor complaints about cuts or song pacing temper the score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean stereo mix, crisp acoustic guitars, strong organ presence. A handful of reviewers note brief drop‑outs (Rain/Snow and early China Cat) but overall the tape is clear and well balanced.

standout_songs: Gathering Flowers for the Master's Bouquet
show_quality.setlist_flow: An impromptu acoustic first set (Bill late) segues into a slower‑to‑fire electric second half; energy ramps up after the early electric songs and peaks with Dark Star → New Speedway Boogie → Lovelight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s classic ’69 guitar tone is praised throughout; his vocals on ‘Gathering Flowers’ and solo work on Dark Star receive high marks.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass comes in strong, especially noticeable during the China/DS jam; a few reviewers note he was late but later locks in solidly.
band_member_comments.Bob: Acoustic guitars are described as clear and “nice”; Bobby’s vocal harmonies (e.g., on ‘Gathering Flowers’) are highlighted as surprisingly on‑key.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ is lauded for texture on Dark Star, New Speedway Boogie, and Lovelight; Pigpen’s organ work also receives specific praise.
